description.narrative:
A guide for Industry to Develop and Update a Competency Standard in targeted industry sectors is developed, along with a series of consultations, awareness raising, and capacity-building activities.
A technical note on Skills Development Funding in Indonesia is produced for the National Development Planning Agency (BAPPENAS), which is a basis for the development of skills development fund in Indonesia. The ILO supported by the Governments of the UK and Japan facilitated the development of the guideline.
The ILO produced and presented the technical notes and as a result, currently, a working group on the formation of SDF was developed by BAPPENAS. The formation of SDF is mandated under the Regulation of the Coordinating Ministry of Human Development and Cultural Affairs no.5/2022 (Permenko PMK no.5/2022).

description.narrative: Four sectoral skills councils on tourism, logistics, ship building, and seafaring have been developed and are ready to be formalised. Sectoral Skills Bodies (called Sectoral Committees in Indonesia) are mandated to be established under the Regulation of the Coordinating Ministry of Human Development and Cultural Affairs no.5/2022 (Permenko PMK no.5/2022. With the support of the Governments of the UK and Japan, the ILO has convened senior participants from government ministries, industry and worker representatives, and academic and vocational experts and leaders, in each of the sectors over the past three years. The ILO provided structured capacity building for these sectoral stakeholders in topics such as sectoral approaches to skills development; the roles of industry in vocational training and education, inclusive skills development, and measuring skills mismatches. A STED (Skills for Trade and Economic Diversification) analysis was undertaken in the sub-sectors of logistics, shipbuilding, and seafaring.
